position: Congressional Action Items (Cap indirect costs at universities)
proposal: The Mandate recommends that Congress cap the indirect (overhead) cost rate the federal government pays universities for research so that it does not exceed the lowest rate a university accepts from a private organization funding research. It presents this as a market-based way to reduce federal subsidy of university overhead.

status_summary: No statute capping university indirect cost rates at a private-funder benchmark has been enacted; instead the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (P.L. 119-75, signed 2026-02-03) carries a bar on HHS developing or implementing a modified approach to indirect cost rates (Div. B sec. 224, per CRS), a grants consultancy summary reports that it also requires DoD to keep its existing rate framework (Div. A sec. 8146), and Public Law 119-103 (approved 2026-09-02) continues the fiscal year 2026 Acts' authority and conditions to 2026-12-11 at the latest, so the bars are inferred to remain in force under the continuing appropriations (an inference from section 101, which does not mention indirect costs). The executive branch pursued a different design, flat 15 percent caps: NIH issued NOT-OD-25-068 on 2025-02-07, DOE, NSF and DoD issued similar caps in April to June 2025, and courts blocked all four (NIH permanent injunction 2025-04-04, affirmed by the First Circuit on 2026-01-05; DOE preliminary injunction 2025-05-15; NSF policy vacated on 2025-06-20; DoD preliminary injunction 2025-07-18, followed by summary judgment for the plaintiffs on 2025-10-10), with a trade-press report of 2026-04-09 that the Justice Department did not seek Supreme Court review of the NIH ruling. The FY2027 budget again proposes a 15 percent NIH cap and removal of the bar. Because Congress, the actor the text names, enacted provisions that keep negotiated rates in place rather than a cap, the record is judged diverged.

A federal judge in Massachusetts permanently barred NIH from applying the 15 percent indirect cost cap, finding it arbitrary and capricious, contrary to statute and adopted without required rulemaking, as reported by Higher Ed Dive.

A federal judge in Massachusetts issued a preliminary injunction barring the DOE 15 percent cap from being applied to any college, as reported by Higher Ed Dive; the date is given in a law firm's note.
The D. Mass. court entered final judgment for the plaintiffs vacating the NSF 15 percent rate and Policy Notice NSF 25-034 and declaring them arbitrary and capricious and contrary to law.

timeline.event: The First Circuit affirmed the NIH ruling (Massachusetts v. NIH, No. 25-1343, with two related appeals), relying on recurring HHS appropriations language and on the Uniform Guidance as adopted at 45 CFR Part 75.
The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 became Public Law 119-75; per CRS, Division B section 224 carries the bar on HHS developing or implementing a modified approach to indirect cost rates.

A grants consultancy summary reported that P.L. 119-75 also requires DoD to keep applying its existing indirect cost rate framework and bars use of funds to change those rates (Div. A sec. 8146), alongside the HHS bar in Div. B sec. 224.
A trade-press report said the Justice Department let the deadline to petition the Supreme Court pass without filing, leaving the January 2026 First Circuit decision on the NIH cap in place.
CRS reported that P.L. 119-75 continues the HHS indirect cost bar and that the FY2027 budget again proposes a 15 percent NIH cap and removal of the bar.

title: Cap federal indirect cost rates for university research at the lowest private-funder rate
uncertainties: The Mandate asks Congress for a cap tied to the lowest rate a university accepts from a private funder; the 15 percent caps are a flat executive cap and are tracked as a parallel design. The section 224 citation rests on CRS and the section 8146 DoD provision on a consultancy summary. The govinfo.gov HTML and PDF of P.L. 119-75 were opened again on 2026-10-22 and still end within Division A (sections 8044 and 8072), so neither provision was read in statutory text; the provisions are uncodified, so no Code page applies. An external retrieval of the official enrolled text, not confirmed by an opened copy, reports the same section numbers and describes Division B section 224 as keeping the 45 CFR part 75 indirect cost provisions in force for NIH as applied in the third quarter of fiscal year 2017 and barring funds from being used to develop or implement a modified approach, in words that may reach funds of HHS or of any department or agency, and Division A section 8146 as requiring DoD to keep applying negotiated rates under 2 CFR 200.414 as applied in fiscal year 2024; the record keeps the HHS wording because section 224 was not opened. The same reading finds no percentage cap and no calendar end date in either section; both sit in the fiscal year 2026 act. Public Law 119-103 (approved 2026-09-02, opened on govinfo.gov) continues funding at fiscal year 2026 rates under the authority and conditions of the listed fiscal year 2026 Acts, which include Public Laws 119-74 and 119-75, until 2026-12-11 at the latest (section 106); that the two bars continue under it is an inference, since Division A mentions no indirect cost rates, and its section 157, which refers to a rule revising the Uniform Guidance, was not examined for any bearing on indirect costs. A fiscal year 2027 appropriations act would decide whether the bars continue beyond that date. The NSF and DoD orders were read on copies hosted by universities, not on a court site; the NIH and DOE district court rulings rest on trade-press reports, with the DOE injunction date of 2025-05-15 given in a law firm's note. A case tracker's docket summary, not confirmed from a court copy, reports a DOE temporary restraining order of 2025-04-16, a final judgment of 2025-06-30 on the government's unopposed motion and an appeal terminated in March 2026; that vacatur is therefore not shown as a court event. The absence of a Supreme Court petition rests on a trade-press report of 2026-04-09 and was not checked on the Supreme Court docket. The remedy wording of the 2025-10-10 DoD order was not read, and whether DoD appealed it was not checked. The stage is a judgment call: blocked 10 is the alternative if the court-halted parallel executive caps are treated as the deciding action, while diverged follows if Congress's re-enacted bar is treated as the deciding action for a congressional ask.
